author: assistant sub-agent V3G8 (v3 re-map); fix pass Fix1

vectors.enisa_quote: Unauthorized access/intrusion into buidlings, premises and sites
vectors.reason: ENISA names intrusion into premises and the affected assets are 'Ground: all assets'; it does not say whose ground systems the intruder then reaches. The weak step is treating a physical intruder as sitting inside the mission's own ground systems.

vectors.enisa_quote: (ground or space, if they are located on the ground)
vectors.reason: ENISA includes space assets that are on the ground, i.e. a spacecraft at an integration or launch site; the intruder then acts on the spacecraft before launch. The weak step is that ENISA never names integration or launch sites.

rows.reason: Insertion of malicious code or data during manufacturing or delivery is the supply-chain compromise of TR55; TR21 describes an intruder at a site.
Poisoned developer dependencies and build tools are a supply-chain method (TR55), not an intrusion into premises.
Software altered before delivery is supply-chain compromise (TR55); TR21 does not describe a delivery step.
Altering boards or programmable logic before delivery is the tainted hardware of TR15; TR21's intruder acts at a site, not on a supplier's parts.
Compromising a software-defined radio is a radio-side route; TR21 describes physical intrusion.
A compromised neighbour satellite over a crosslink is not an intrusion into premises.
A secondary communication path is not mentioned; TR21 describes physical intrusion.
A backup or alternate ground station is not mentioned; the text names buildings, premises and sites in general.
The backup RF receive path is not mentioned in TR21.
Orbital rendezvous is the rogue-object approach of TR18; TR21's spacecraft are on the ground.
Analysing a spacecraft's emissions from a nearby vehicle is the spying of TR18; TR21 describes intrusion into sites.
Docking or OSAM capture is the docked-vehicle connection of TR20; TR21's spacecraft are on the ground.
Grappling with a capture mechanism is an in-orbit contact method; TR21's assets are on the ground.
A hosted payload as a door into the bus is not mentioned in TR21.

rows.enisa_quote: compromise, modification, damage to or even theft of the satellite lifecycle assets
rows.sparta_quote: Compromising the ground segment gives an adversary the most direct path to first execution
rows.reason: Intrusion into a ground site leads to compromise of ground-located assets; SPARTA's ground-system foothold is the closest description (a physical intruder is modelled as a ground compromise). Ground-asset damage and theft have no SPARTA technique, so this vector is entry-only by design.
Tampering with the on-orbit update pipeline is a specific later step; ENISA names no update manipulation.
Sending commands through a valid ground station is a specific later step; ENISA names no commanding.
Rogue External Entity is an RF foothold from outside; TR21 describes physical intrusion.
A rogue ground station transmitting mission signals is not an intrusion into premises.
Rogue Spacecraft is an RF peer in orbit; TR21's assets are on the ground.
A counterspace weapon is the ASAT case of TR18; TR21 describes intrusion into sites.
A trusted relationship is not mentioned; TR21's intruder is unauthorized.
Mission collaborators as access route are not mentioned in TR21.
Vendor access is the supply-chain relationship of TR55; TR21's intruder is unauthorized, not a vendor.
End-user equipment as attacker origin is not mentioned in TR21.
Timing first execution to safe-mode is not described.
Plugging a peripheral or removable medium into equipment is the rogue-device connection of TR20; TR21 states intrusion into sites, not a device.

rows.sparta_quote: compromised laptops or transient cyber assets push images and tables
rows.reason: An intruder at an assembly, test or launch site meets the spacecraft where tools and flight interfaces connect; ATLO compromise is the SPARTA technique for access to a spacecraft on the ground.
The host spacecraft as a door into a hosted payload is not mentioned in TR21.
ENISA gives no spacecraft function that is abused; its outcomes are for assets located on the ground.
No state or mode change of a spacecraft is described; outcomes concern assets located on the ground.
'Modification' of assets is stated without saying that settings are changed.
'Modification' is stated for assets, without saying that data is falsified or deleted.
No change to command or data flow is described.

rows.enisa_quote: modification, damage to or even theft of the satellite lifecycle assets
rows.sparta_quote: the deliberate alteration of the implementation that controls spacecraft behavior
rows.reason: 'Modification' of a space asset located on the ground is read as altered flight software or firmware; this is an interpretation, because modification of a physical asset is not necessarily code. Physical damage and theft have no SPARTA technique.
No depletion of a resource is described.
No clock or synchronisation change is described.
Pivoting from a hosted payload into the host is not described by TR21.
Hopping between satellites over a crosslink is not described by TR21.

Physical damage and theft have no SPARTA technique (sparta_gap) and are not coded.

review_response.finding: Wrong origin class: space assets on the ground at sites; proximity/supply_chain not considered, IA-0012/IA-0011 missing

IA-0011 is D-OTHER to TR20. Candidate files for TR21 now include all entries, so IA-0005.x, IA-0011, IA-0012 were assessed.

review_response.action: kept because no closer SPARTA technique exists; the row reason and vector reason say physical intrusion is modelled as ground compromise (vector basis 'weak').
